S.FORM: sua napalaŋa kisa-i caau ia, tee=ku pu-a-kari-kari.
S.PHON: sua napaɾaŋa kisai ʦaau ia teeku puakarikari
S.FORM: sua naparanga kisai caau ia, teeku puakarikari.
S.PHON: sua napa[r|ɾ]aŋa kisai ʦaau ia teeku puaka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: I'm going to talk about the place which people call Napalanga.
I am Mu'u.

S.FORM: sua pu-a-iisua napalaŋa kisa-ən ia, ma-kaasi mia canpi=kani ia, kaʔan=kia taavalaʔə mia-sua kin-u-ʔucaŋ-a=kara=ʔai ma-naasə alu-paka-ləəvə=kara.
S.PHON: sua puaiisua napaɾaŋa kisaən ia makaaʂi mia ʦanpikani ia kaʔankia taavaɾaʔə miasua kinuʔuʦaŋakaraʔai manaasə aɾupakaɾəəvəkara
S.FORM: sua puaiisua naparanga kisaen ia, makaasi mia canpikani ia, ka'ankia taavara'e miasua kinu'ucangakara'ai manaase arupakareevekara.
S.PHON: sua puaiisua napa[r|ɾ]aŋa kisaen ia makaaʂi mia ʦanpikani ia kaʔankia taava[r|ɾ]aʔe miasua kinuʔuʦaŋaka[r|ɾ]aʔai manaase a[r|ɾ]upaka[r|ɾ]eeveka[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: I will talk about Napalanga for the first time, I don't know whether they were a couple or friends at that time.

S.FORM: sua iisua ia, maraa kuu=kia a-manəŋ.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia maraa kuukia amanəŋ
S.FORM: sua iisua ia, maraa kuukia amaneng.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia ma[r|ɾ]aa kuukia amaneŋ
S.TRANSL: As for that, I did not quite get it well.

S.FORM: sua taavalaʔə=naku ia, kin-a-laʔəv-a mu-kusa=kan na təanəkai ʔita-ʔitan napalaŋa iisa.
S.PHON: sua taavaɾaʔənaku ia kinaɾaʔəva mukusakan na təanəkai ʔitaʔitan napaɾaŋa iisa
S.FORM: sua taavara'enaku ia, kinara'eva mukusakan na teanekai 'ita'itan naparanga iisa.
S.PHON: sua taava[r|ɾ]aʔenaku ia kina[r|ɾ]aʔeva mukusakan na teanekai ʔitaʔitan napa[r|ɾ]aŋa iisa
S.TRANSL: I know that the couple went to the top of the cliff in Napalanga.
They discussed, "What shall we do?"
"We shall fall down," the woman said.
The man said, "Let's do what you decided (said)."

S.FORM: makasua=cu mu-ʔuna ʔinia maa-kari, ʔənava cəpəŋə tia=mata-paliʔi.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muʔuna ʔinia maakari ʔənava ʦəpəŋə tiamatapaɾiʔi
makasuaʦu muʔuna ʔinia maaka[r|ɾ]i ʔenava ʦepeŋe tiamatapa[r|ɾ]iʔi
S.TRANSL: After they discussed, it turned out that they decided to fall down.

S.FORM: "nakai a-pa-taa-sana kuvari iikasu-ini kəəcə nanakə mu-ʔulu-ʔulu m-usu-tupuku," misa=kani.
S.PHON: nakai apataasana kuvari iikasuini kəəʦə nanakə muʔuɾuʔuɾu musutupuku misakani
S.FORM: "nakai apataasana kuvari iikasuini keece nanake mu'uru'uru musutupuku," misakani.
S.PHON: nakai apataasana kuva[r|ɾ]i iikasuini keeʦe nanake muʔu[r|ɾ]uʔu[r|ɾ]u musutupuku misakani
S.TRANSL: "You may decide to turn down and you do first," (the man) said.

S.FORM: ma-kaasi=kani sua nanakə, "iikasu-ini maa-kai-naanu?" misa=kani nanakə.
S.PHON: makaaʂikani sua nanakə iikasuini maakainaanu misakani nanakə
S.FORM: makaasikani sua nanake, "iikasuini maakainaanu?" misakani nanake.
S.PHON: makaaʂikani sua nanake iikasuini maakainaanu misakani nanake
S.TRANSL: Similarly, the woman said, "How about you (man fall down first?)"
They discussed (who should fall down first).
"You man (can try first)," she said to the man.

S.FORM: ma-kaasi=cu=kani saruanai, "makasua-ini ia, iiku=ʔai mu-ʔulu-ʔulu," misa=kani.
S.PHON: makaaʂiʦukani saruanai makasuaini ia iikuʔai muʔuɾuʔuɾu misakani
S.FORM: makaasicukani saruanai, "makasuaini ia, iiku'ai mu'uru'uru," misakani.
S.PHON: makaaʂiʦukani sa[r|ɾ]uanai makasuaini ia iikuʔai muʔu[r|ɾ]uʔu[r|ɾ]u misakani
S.TRANSL: Consequently the man said, "Perhaps I shall fall down first."

S.FORM: "tee=kasu maa-kai-naanu mu-ʔulu-ʔulu ni-pivəra?" misa=kani sua saruanai.
S.PHON: teekasu maakainaanu muʔuɾuʔuɾu nipivəra misakani sua saruanai
S.FORM: "teekasu maakainaanu mu'uru'uru nipivera?" misakani sua saruanai.
S.PHON: teekasu maakainaanu muʔu[r|ɾ]uʔu[r|ɾ]u nipive[r|ɾ]a misakani sua sa[r|ɾ]uanai
S.TRANSL: "How can you go down first because you're pregnant?" the man said.
"Yes," the woman said.

S.FORM: makaa-sua=cu sua saruanai mu-kusa=kani təa-təanəkai ʔitan, napalaŋa iisa.
S.PHON: makaasuaʦu sua saruanai mukusakani təatəanəkai ʔitan napaɾaŋa iisa
S.FORM: makaasuacu sua saruanai mukusakani teateanekai 'itan, naparanga iisa.
S.PHON: makaasuaʦu sua sa[r|ɾ]uanai mukusakani teateanekai ʔitan napa[r|ɾ]aŋa iisa
S.TRANSL: Consequently, the man went to the top of the cliff in Napalanga.
"Just look at me," the man said.
"Yes," his wife said.

S.FORM: tee=cu=kani m-i-ŋanai, mu-ciri ia, "c<əm>əʔəra-a ʔikua!" kisa-ən=kani=kiai ʔucaŋ-in.
S.PHON: teeʦukani miŋanai mutʂiri ia ʦəməʔəraa ʔikua kisaənkanikiai ʔuʦaŋin
teeʦukani miŋanai mutʂi[r|ɾ]i ia ʦemeʔe[r|ɾ]aa ʔikua kisaenkanikiai ʔuʦaŋin
S.TRANSL: When he was standing about to jump down, "Look at me!" he said to his wife.
His wife was standing up to follow him.
The man jumped down.
He flew down like a bird.

S.FORM: tara-uka-ai=kani ʔucaŋ-in, kuu=kani=kiai timan-ai kaa-kulu-kuluŋ si m-ari-ŋəcai.
S.PHON: taraukaaikani ʔuʦaŋin kuukanikiai timanai kaakuɾukuɾuŋ ʂi mariŋəʦai
S.FORM: taraukaaikani 'ucangin, kuukanikiai timanai kaakurukurung si maringecai.
S.PHON: ta[r|ɾ]aukaaikani ʔuʦaŋin kuukanikiai timanai kaaku[r|ɾ]uku[r|ɾ]uŋ ʂi ma[r|ɾ]iŋeʦai
S.TRANSL: His wife could not see him or hear any sound because she still was high up there.

S.FORM: taavalaʔə=cu ʔucaŋ-in kan ʔeesi=cu ʔənə-ʔənai misa=kani.
S.PHON: taavaɾaʔəʦu ʔuʦaŋin kan ʔeeʂiʦu ʔənəʔənai misakani
taava[r|ɾ]aʔeʦu ʔuʦaŋin kan ʔeeʂiʦu ʔeneʔenai misakani
S.TRANSL: His wife knew that he must have plunged into the ground (and died).
"I shall come along (with you)," his wife said.
She was pregnant.
His wife went following him, and jumped down after him.
(She) jumped down after him.
Her husband was on the ground.
The man disappeared and he had been broken into pieces.
As for his wife, she was pregnant.
When she fell down on the ground, her legs were stretching out apart.
She was standing, being pregnant, she did not fall down lying (on the ground).
Because she did not fall down lying (on the ground), she went home and gave birth to a baby.

S.FORM: iimu sua napalaŋa kisa-ən ia, ara-anai=cu ʔinia.
S.PHON: iimu sua napaɾaŋa kisaən ia araanaiʦu ʔinia
S.FORM: iimu sua naparanga kisaen ia, araanaicu 'inia.
S.PHON: iimu sua napa[r|ɾ]aŋa kisaen ia a[r|ɾ]aanaiʦu ʔinia
S.TRANSL: (The baby was born) in Napalanga, therefore (the baby would be named) based on it.
According to the people's words, it was called Tapukul (name in Bunun).

S.FORM: sua tapukul kisa-ən ia, ʔaisi ʔinia ŋanai=mia ka-vaŋvaŋ.
S.PHON: sua tapukuɾ kisaən ia ʔaiʂi ʔinia ŋanaimia kavaŋvaŋ
S.FORM: sua tapukur kisaen ia, 'aisi 'inia nganaimia kavangvang.
S.PHON: sua tapuku[r|ɾ] kisaen ia ʔaiʂi ʔinia ŋanaimia kavaŋvaŋ
S.TRANSL: All our names are covered by the place, name Tapukul.

S.FORM: sua tapukul kisa-ən naa ni-usu-tupuk-a kin-u-ʔucaŋ-a iisa.
S.PHON: sua tapukuɾ kisaən naa niusutupuka kinuʔuʦaŋa iisa
S.FORM: sua tapukur kisaen naa niusutupuka kinu'ucanga iisa.
S.PHON: sua tapuku[r|ɾ] kisaen naa niusutupuka kinuʔuʦaŋa iisa
S.TRANSL: Tapukul was where the couple had fallen down.
I can only tell you this much.
Listen to my words carefully.

S.FORM: caniava nu naini iikita nuari tara-vəavəa ara-siŋsiŋ ia, tavalaʔ-ən=kiai ka-vaŋəvaŋə makasua ava.
S.PHON: ʦaniava nu naini iikita nuari taravəavəa araʂiŋʂiŋ ia tavaɾaʔənkiai kavaŋəvaŋə makasua ava
S.FORM: caniava nu naini iikita nuari taraveavea arasingsing ia, tavara'enkiai kavangevange makasua ava.
S.PHON: ʦaniava nu naini iikita nua[r|ɾ]i ta[r|ɾ]aveavea a[r|ɾ]aʂiŋʂiŋ ia tava[r|ɾ]aʔenkiai kavaŋevaŋe makasua ava
S.TRANSL: For example, if any of us is still alive and healthy next year, all people will know the truth.

S.PHON: sua niusutupuka iisua ia napaɾaŋa kisaən
sua niusutupuka iisua ia napa[r|ɾ]aŋa kisaen
S.TRANSL: The place where they fell down was called "Napalanga" (in Kanakanavu).
It is called "Tapukul" in Bunun.

S.FORM: sua iikita kanakanavu ia, napalaŋa misai=kita.
S.PHON: sua iikita kanakanavu ia napaɾaŋa misaikita
S.FORM: sua iikita kanakanavu ia, naparanga misaikita.
S.PHON: sua iikita kanakanavu ia napa[r|ɾ]aŋa misaikita
S.TRANSL: In our Kanakanavu, we call it Napalanga.
In Bunun, it is called Tapukul.

S.FORM: makasua maamia sua si-a-tuuturu=maku kamua ma-manu=maku.
S.PHON: makasua maamia sua ʂiatuuturumaku kamua mamanumaku
S.FORM: makasua maamia sua siatuuturumaku kamua mamanumaku.
S.PHON: makasua maamia sua ʂiatuutu[r|ɾ]umaku kamua mamanumaku
S.TRANSL: I can only tell you, my young people this much.
Stay healthy! Thank you.
